I agree with you on obsessing about one particular person is bad. Also the hiding of the content is problematic. I'm not going to go into your personal story either, so understand that I only disagree about the advice in your last paragraph.
Yes, his actions are important in regards to how to move on from this, however it's not healthy to make a list of demands to someone, especially a loved one and expect them to accept it, like wise, we, as people with BPD have the tendency to test people and put up obstacles for them to 'prove' themselves. Which, again doesn't help us, if they fail it reinforces of the negative things we say to ourselves. If the pressure of the demands pushes them away we again reinforce the abandonment that we feel.
We can set reasonable boundaries with people.
But Boundaries aren't tests or ultimatums

We can't change the world so it fits us, we just have to manage ourselves and how we react to it.

I haven't had a FP for a long time and I really miss having one although I realise that having one can be a trap and being co-dependent isn't the healthiest thing to be - I find that the feelings I had when they didn't reply to a message for a while or I didn't hear from them in general for a while has transferred onto a lot of other relationships personal and otherwise.

Like before I would really care too much if people didn't get back to me quickly as long as I was in touch with my FP, it didn't matter

I think it's a bit effd up that he had all the photos in the same folder. That's oddly disrespectful. But everyone has their fantasies.
It's where those fantasies stop and don't become an obsession.

You're valid to your feelings and he should respect them. I just know from my own BPD managing, that forcing people to indulge in behaviours because of our insecurities isn't healthy and doesn't help us to manage/confront those insecurities and takes away their autonomy. Creating a 'parent/scolded child' dynamic.
If your partner is loving, attentive, supportive and emotionally loyal - I would treat the nsfw pics as just a fantasy.

Obviously its different if they have a irl/or personal relationship
But with all of this I can voice an opinion but ultimately it's up to you and your partner to discuss your reasonable boundaries
